summary: At just 6.8 square miles, Antelope packs nearly 50,000 people into a density north of 7,200 per square mile — denser than many parts of Sacramento proper, yet the landscape reads as pure suburban subdivision: flat Sacramento Valley floor, no downtown core, no walkable commercial strip, and streets that dead-end into cul-de-sacs rather than connecting into a grid. That flatness delivers enormous sky and reliable sunshine — averaging 9.4 hours of sun per day, with summer highs pushing well into the 90s and mild winters rarely dipping below the low 40s at night. Antelope functions overwhelmingly as a bedroom community; major employers sit south along the I-80 corridor and in downtown Sacramento, roughly a 20-to-30-minute drive without traffic, though commute times balloon on Highway 99 and Interstate 80 during peak hours. A median home value around $468,000 against a median household income near $95,100 puts the price-to-income ratio just under 5:1 — tight but within conventional lending reach without requiring dual six-figure earners, and median rent at $2,063 consumes roughly 26% of that gross income. Grocery and dining options cluster along Elverta Road and Antelope Road in strip-mall format rather than any pedestrian-friendly center. Antelope is the kind of place where the financial math works better than the walkability, and whether that tradeoff suits you depends entirely on how much of your life happens inside a car.
